articles.title: Sweaty, triumphant and decked out in neon: I asked NYC Marathon runners what they wore – in pictures
articles.summary: On 1 November, 61,000 people ran in the 2026 New York City Marathon. We asked about the running gear – and motivations – that carried them to the finish line. The best women’s running shoes for roads and trails.
body: The sea of orange thermal blankets, shiny medals and brightly colored running shoes is impossible to miss.
On 1 November, 61,000 people took over New York City’s streets for the 2026 NYC Marathon. Making it through the 26.2-mile race is a feat that takes grit, endurance and … the right gear.

Near Central Park, blocks from the finish line, I navigated swarms of proud parents and groups holding neon posters emblazoned “hot girls run marathons”, asking runners about their sneakers, energy fuel and shorts. (It turns out Nike Alphaflys are a marathon favorite.) When I couldn’t find exact matches for their items, I linked to brands with similar options.

From a 71-year-old who has run the NYC Marathon over 30 times to an Olympic trial qualifier who placed seventh in her age group – marathoners also shared what brought them to the starting line, with stories that remind us there is more than one way to be a runner, and just as many reasons to keep showing up.
points: On 1 November, 61,000 people ran in the 2026 New York City Marathon.
We asked about the running gear – and motivations – that carried them to the finish line.

articles.title: A job that changed me: I ran observatory tours as a student. An eight-year-old’s question taught me two important lessons
articles.summary: I thought the explanation I’d given about black holes was family-friendly. But, after what she had said, I had to rethink my examples. In the first year of my science degree, I was fortunate to land a job as an astronomy guide at the Sydney Observatory.
body: My favourite object to show in the planetarium was the Hubble Ultra Deep Field image. Before revealing the image, I’d explain how the Hubble space telescope had stared at a piece of sky the size of a grain of sand held at arm’s length for 11 days, collecting enough light to look into the farthest corners of the universe. Then I’d zoom in on that tiny piece of sky, revealing the gorgeous image. At least one person would audibly gasp at the reveal.

But I wasn’t done. I’d get them to spot the spiky objects in the image. There were four obvious stars that were part of our galaxy, the Milky Way. I’d seal the existential crisis by saying: “Those spiky objects are stars. Everything else you see in this image, every blob, every smudge, every tiny speck … is a galaxy.”

On one tour, the clouds were not working with us. So, after showing the group the “stars” through the telescope – the stars on the Australian flag hoisted atop the Sydney Harbour Bridge – I led us down to the 3D theatre. Eventually, the imagination and curiosity of the group took us to the topic of black holes.

articles.title: The pet I’ll never forget: the tiny horse with a big personality – who helps psychiatric patients
articles.summary: Black Pearl is a therapy animal, who works with military veterans. This sweet show-off has completely changed my life. I trained and competed in dressage for many years and after I retired, I decided to buy a miniature horse for company at home in southern California.
body: I started training her for fun and began to teach her tricks. She learned quickly. I thought of a great way to give back to the community – Black Pearl and I could find ways to help people. I started to wonder where I could visit with my little horse.

Black Pearl inspired me to start my charity, Mini Therapy Horses. If it wasn’t for her outgoing personality, I wouldn’t have attempted it. Now I run a programme with her and eight other miniature therapy horses, visiting patients in the lockdown psychiatric unit at a veterans’ hospital in Los Angeles. The vets have been through so much: they have PTSD, traumatic brain injuries and/or drug addiction and many are homeless. They can pet and hug the horses – they love them. It helps them to feel less lonely and isolated.

We also visit several other hospitals – many of the kids and adults are away from home for a long time and the time they spend with our minis is very comforting. If a child is visually impaired we can take their hands and help them to feel our little horses. They can brush their coats and this tactile experience makes them very happy.

articles.title: Beyond the Iconic Potato Dish at New NYC Restaurant Somssi
articles.summary: You’ve probably heard of the Potato Potato Potato dish at Somssi, the newest restaurant from Na:eun Hospitality. The triple-layered potato dish is the most labor-intensive dish on the menu but has also become the most popular order, with the kitchen going through up to 100 pounds of potatoes each…
body: Yukon gold potatoes are put through a ricer to become a cream and butter-heavy puree that is set in molds in the freezer. After being toasted in breadcrumbs, the logs of potato are wrapped in russet potato ribbons before being fried up to order.

Next is the ox tongue, which is brined for just over 16 hours before being slow-cooked in herbs, aromatics, and beef tallow for four hours. Huge cuts of tongue are carefully scored so they will get a great sear when they hit the grill. It’s served on a romesco sauce with just a bit of wasabi on the side.

Finally, pork loin is coated in ground shrimp for a creative schnitzel that is reminiscent of shrimp toast. The schnitzel is topped with a sweet-and-sour plum sauce that balances out the thick, crispy fried exterior. Scallop crudo is made up of pressed scallops surrounded with a strawberry sauce and topped off with gooseberries and peppers.
Watch the team at Somssi create creative dishes like a triple-potato bite and a show-stopping grilled tongue dish in this episode of Mise En Place.

articles.title: The Best Dressed Stars at the 2026 CFDA Awards
articles.summary: The red carpet was full of celebrities in the best of American fashion.
body: Tonight, the 2026 CFDA Awards brought out the the best and brightest in American style. A-listers and industry insiders alike gathered together at the American Museum of Natural History in New York City to honor fashion’s foremost innovators and creators. The awards are always a great moment for recognizing the brands leading the pack now, and a bellwether for which emerging designers are set to take off in the year ahead. With actress Keke Palmer hosting, the show itself promised to be a thoroughly entertaining affair.

But, before the honors were handed out—including, the international designer of the year award to Anthony Vaccarello, the lifetime achievement award to photographers Inez van Lamsweerde and Vinoodh Matadin, and the icon award to architect Peter Marino—stars, editors, designers, and their muses hit the red carpet. Many opted for the classics, or pared-back, monochromatic attire. But, a few standout gold looks added some sparkle. Predictably, there was a strong contingent of stars in Vaccarello’s Saint Laurent. Hailey Bieber, Zoë Kravitz, Anja Rubik, and Rosé glittered in pieces from his latest, and last, collection for the brand.

articles.title: 9 Best Scalp Shampoos for Your Scalp to Help Dryness, Flakiness, and Sensitivity
articles.summary: The best shampoos for your scalp give a thorough cleanse without adding more irritation. Here, experts break down their favorite scalp shampoos by Aveeno, Nizoral, Briogeo, and more.
body: Dermatologists always recommend a good shampoo for the scalp to give it a thorough cleanse. But which one depends on your specific needs and how well your skin will tolerate certain ingredients. “I wouldn't choose a shampoo simply because it says, ‘ sulfate-free,’” adds Dr. King. “The important question is whether the overall surfactant system effectively cleans without irritating your particular scalp.”

“Shampoos with effective surfactants are best for cleaning the scalp,” says Dr. King. Some of those surfactants she says to look for include sulfates like sodium lauryl sulfate (SLS) and sodium laureth sulfate (SLES), but you can look for gentler ones like sodium methyl cocoyl taurate.

Dr. Erickson says that if you’re dealing with a dry scalp, you’ll want to skip harsher surfactants like sulfates, and fragrance to minimize irritation. Instead, look for hydrating, barrier repairing ingredients like ceramides, niacinamide, glycerin, and panthenol to pair with gentle surfactants or exfoliators.
points: The best shampoos for your scalp give a thorough cleanse without adding more irritation.

articles.title: 17 Trips You Should Book a Year in Advance
articles.summary: It's never too early for planning a trip a year in advance. It just gives you something to look forward to.
body: I'm a firm believer that holidays need a balance of organization and freedom, so that you can enjoy all the long-awaited activities without feeling like they're obligations. Starting to organize and book excursions well in advance can make your experience considerably better, especially when planning trips to particularly popular destinations. Though, that's not the only reason why you should already be thinking about what to add to your 2027 travel bucket list.

Planning a trip a year in advance, long before your suitcase ever leaves the closet, offers up a very particular and potent type of dopamine hit. The moment you confirm a flight or secure a coveted reservation delivers its own quiet thrill, a reminder that the joy of travel lives not only in the trip itself, but in the anticipation that precedes it.
